text:
Berkly Catton is the most interesting thing happening in Seattle. The 20-year-old has become the Kraken's offensive leader, with a hat trick against Vancouver that Sportsnaut broke down as a forecheck clinic, and Daily Faceoff wondered whether he "might be the game-breaking talent the Kraken need." His line with Shane Wright and Kaapo Kakko is where Seattle's future sits, and Kakko (8 points in his last 10, including a late winner against Anaheim) is riding along nicely.

The rest of the picture is a team outplaying its talent level on the scoreboard and not on the ice. Seattle is 12-10-1, but it gets only 46% of the expected goals and 45% at five on five, and it has scored about six more goals than its chances deserve. Our numbers say the Kraken have about three more points than they earned. Lane Lambert's top pairs both lose the shot battle badly: Adam Larsson and Vince Dunn get 42% of the expected goals, Brandon Montour and Ryker Evans 48%, though both pairs have won on goals. The Jordan Eberle, Chandler Stephenson and Bobby McMann line is at 39%, and McMann has 2 points in his last 10.

Our numbers give Seattle a 33% chance at the playoffs after a 4-6-0 stretch. What we'd watch: how much the coaching staff hands Catton and Wright, because a team this far behind on chances needs its young skill to tilt the ice, not just finish.
